zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving case and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When outputting attribute values in the final JSON solution.
zebralogic.example: Outputting 'boba tea' as 'Boba Tea' or 'bobaTea' would be incorrect.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues that state "X is directly left of Y" as X's house number = Y's house number − 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing adjacency clues with a specified direction.
zebralogic.example: Treating "X is directly left of Y" as merely "X is left of Y" (allowing any distance) would be too permissive.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: Treat clues that say "X is somewhere to the left of Y" as a strict ordering constraint X < Y.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing ordering clues without adjacency information.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "X is somewhere to the left of Y" as "X is immediately left of Y" would be overly restrictive.

zebralogic.title: AdjacencyWithoutOrientation
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues that state "X and Y are next to each other" as |X − Y| = 1, with no implied left/right.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing adjacency clues that do not specify direction.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X is left of Y when the clue only says they are next to each other would add an unwarranted ordering constraint.

zebralogic.title: ExactDistance
zebralogic.principle: For clues stating "There are N houses between X and Y", enforce |X − Y| = N + 1.
zebralogic.example: Treating "one house between X and Y" as "X and Y are adjacent" would violate the intended spacing.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two attributes refer to the same entity, treat them as a combined attribute (they occupy the same house).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing equivalence clues before any ordering or distance reasoning.
zebralogic.example: Failing to link "milk" with "gray hair" would treat them as separate entities and break the puzzle.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, assign that attribute to that house immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly mentions a house number for an attribute.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring "the person who likes milk is in the fourth house" would leave the drink unanchored.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceSubstitutionBeforeOrderingAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Before applying ordering or adjacency constraints, replace any attribute reference with the concrete attribute it is linked to via equivalence, so constraints operate on concrete values.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After processing equivalence clues and before handling ordering/adjacency constraints.
zebralogic.example: Applying "Alice is right of auburn hair" without first substituting the concrete house of auburn hair would leave the constraint ambiguous.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Ensure the final JSON output is syntactically valid: all arrays and objects are properly closed, keys are correct, and the structure matches the expected schema.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After constructing the solution, before returning the answer.
zebralogic.example: Missing a closing bracket or using the wrong top‑level key would cause the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: ChildAttributeLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue mentions a child's name (e.g., "the person whose child is named X"), treat X as the value of a child attribute linked to the parent, not as a separate person.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing clues that involve children or parent‑child relationships.
zebralogic.example: Treating the child's name as an independent person would duplicate a name and break the uniqueness constraint.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may normalize case or alter punctuation when copying values from the problem statement.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy each attribute value verbatim, preserving the original case and any punctuation.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model can focus on a subset of clues and forget to enforce all of them.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Systematically enumerate every clue, translate each into a concrete constraint, and verify that all are satisfied before finalising the grid.

zebralogic.description: Missing required top‑level keys in output JSON
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may omit keys like "reasoning" or "solution" when constructing the final answer.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Always include the top‑level keys "reasoning" and "solution" (or the exact schema required) in the output JSON.

zebralogic.description: Malformed JSON due to missing closing brackets
zebralogic.why_it_happens: During generation the model can lose track of nested structures, especially when the answer is long.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After generation, double‑check that every opening bracket/brace has a matching closing one; use a validator if needed.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may treat a child's name as a separate entity instead of an attribute of the parent.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions a child, bind the child's name to a child attribute of the referenced parent person.
